correctness.rationale: Coordinate swap averages any positive definite Euclidean Q to E_t²=(x+y)²+t(x-y)². For p>2, tau=2^(-2/p) lies in (1/2,1). Same-sign ratio is R_p(r;t)=4(1+t r²)/[(1+r)^p+(1-r)^p]^(2/p); opposite-sign is R_inf(s;t)=4(s²+t)/(1+s)². At t=tau, the opposite sector has exact min 4tau/(1+tau) and max 4tau; sharp two-variable l_p/l2 comparisons place the whole same-sign sector between those bounds. For arbitrary 0<t≤1, its minimum at s=t and diagonal/anti-diagonal contacts force distortion ≥1+tau; for t≥1 the opposite-sector endpoints force D≥2>1+tau. Thus d_BM²=1+2^(-2/p), with displayed ellipse. Published James J=1+2^(-1/p) yields d_BM²=1+(J-1)².
